obligations.text: `update <module> [<version>]` moves an installed module to a newer version and runs its update steps.

obligations.text: Without a version, update moves to the latest available version.
obligations.cases: update with vs without a version; offers 1.1.0 and 1.2.0
obligations.basis: new:iteration-72 (review-71 A2)
obligations.gap: Update without a version calls Install (Main.cls:4445-4449), whose choice versions.rs::installed computes from the offered versions (Main.cls:2603 takes GetAt(1) of the SQL-ordered results). With releases only the order is semantic (releases_agree). With prereleases enabled fixture_neighbors shows the install picks 2.0.0-beta.1 while the semantic maximum is 2.0.0, which refutes "latest". The Update -> Install routing is source reading only, and no theorem states the installed version after update.

obligations.text: -path <archive> updates from a local archive instead of a repository.
obligations.cases: update -path archive vs repository
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70
obligations.gap: update_steps.rs Source::Path only affects the DeveloperMode parameter; archive extraction and loading are not modeled. Contrast: update m -path m-1.2.0.tgz installs the archive payload without a repository.

obligations.text: IPM refuses an update when -DPermitDowngrade is given.
obligations.cases: update with vs without -DPermitDowngrade
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70
obligations.gap: No model of the PermitDowngrade guard in Main.cls::Update. Contrast: update m 1.2.0 -DPermitDowngrade=1 is refused before any history row; without the flag it proceeds.

obligations.text: IPM refuses an update when the -path archive holds a different module from the one named.
obligations.cases: update A -path <B archive> vs <A archive>
obligations.observation: status, error, namespace and ModuleRoot after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70
obligations.gap: No model. Per metadata (D16) the as-built path crashes with <INVALID OREF> in LoadNewModule before the mismatch check, and B's archive stays unpacked under ModuleRoot; neither the intended refusal nor the crash is modeled.

obligations.text: Like a refused load, a refused update keeps no module data.
obligations.cases: each refusal reason vs a successful update
obligations.observation: module records, documents and step records after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70
obligations.gap: end_refused (database equal to the starting state) covers the not-installed and downgrade refusals only. The PermitDowngrade and -path mismatch refusals are not modeled, and for the mismatch the archive left under ModuleRoot (D16) is outside the database model.

obligations.text: `update` does not pass developer mode on to dependencies.
obligations.cases: update -dev of a parent with a registry dependency (release vs snapshot) and a directory dependency
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70
obligations.gap: param_dev models the DeveloperMode parameter of one LoadNewModule run by source and kind, but update_steps has no dependency loads under an update, so no rule contrasts the parent's -dev with its dependencies' mode. param_dev gives a snapshot registry dependency developer mode under -dev, which would contradict the block if update passes -dev down; the update caller's removal of the parameter (CHANGELOG #1036) is not modeled.

obligations.text: `update` checks version requirements against the versions modules will have after the update, not the ones installed now.
obligations.cases: installed module requiring the old version of a co-updated module
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70
obligations.gap: dep_resolve excludes known/co-updating modules from the installed-requirement check (g.known is an input) and proves soundness, but no witness contrasts update with install on the same namespace; how Main.cls::Update populates the co-updating set is not modeled (iter31 states co-updating exclusion is not represented).

obligations.text: Shared dependencies that must move in lock-step update together instead of failing.
obligations.cases: two modules sharing a dependency that both require at new versions
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70
obligations.gap: No model of the lock-step co-update (BuildDependencyGraph with co-updating modules, Update.cls TestSharedTransitiveDependencyUpdate). Contrast: updating A where shared dependency S must move from 1.x to 2.x together with B succeeds rather than failing the installed-requirement check.

obligations.text: Each V<major> class in the update package lists its step methods in order; update walks classes ascending, the all-member list before the primary-only list, each in author order.

obligations.basis: new:iteration-70; iteration-72 rule-4a re-audit (G2): partial, support mutation-checked (mutations G2-m59)
obligations.gap: Rule 4a (iteration-72): The walk order (classes ascending, all-member list before primary-only, author order) is the premise wf on the input step sequence; inst_ok_update_runs_in_walk_order only shows the log follows the given sequence, and class_list (class-number map) is not connected to the walk. Weakening wf to distinct keys (G2-m59) fails only the helper inst_lemma_flag_step, which needs class contiguity for the newStepToApply flag: the order is assumed there, not derived.
